To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the mTOR kinase is a critical point of crosstalk between GPCR and insulin/IGF1 signaling systems and 2) metformin, an FDA-approved anti-diabetic drug, can be used to target mTOR and inhibit pancreatic cancer cell growth.

insulin/IGF1 receptor signaling and G protein-couple receptor signaling converge on mTOR in PDAC cells, and that targeting mTOR in pancreatic cancer cells with metformin is an important strategy for the chemoprevention and treatment of PDAC.

insulin/IGF1 receptor signaling, via activation of the mTORC1 pathway, promotes the growth of pancreatic cancer cells and that this signaling system is also a point of convergence between GPCR signaling and the insulin/IGFs.
In summary, our research is concerned with

understanding the mechanisms that regulate cell growth in response to insulin and IGF-1, with an emphasis on how the insulin/IGFs and heptahedral GPCRs signal through a common downstream effector, mTOR, to promote pancreatic cancer cell growth.

the role of mTOR in mediating cAMP signaling in PDAC cells, with a focus on the role of the GPCR-coupled receptor for prostaglandin E2 (EP2), and the potential for targeting the insulin/IGFR/mTOR pathway as a novel approach for PDAC chemoprevention.
identifying the mechanisms that link obesity and T2DM with the development and progression of PDAC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
insulin, IGF-1 and GPCRs are important modifiable risk factors in PDAC and that targeting the mTOR signaling system may be an effective strategy in the chemoprevention of PDAC.
insulin/IGF and GPCRs are important in PDAC development, and mTOR is a key signaling molecule that links the two signaling pathways.
mTOR is a point of convergence between insulin/IGFI signaling and GPCR-mediated signaling in pancreatic cancer cell lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mTOR is a key convergence point for insulin/IGF and GPCR signaling systems and is a promising target in pancreatic cancer cells.

the insulin receptor, IGF-1 receptor, and GPCRs converge on the mTOR pathway to promote pancreatic cancer development and that metformin, an mTOR inhibitor, may be useful in the chemoprevention of PDAC.
mTOR is a key point of convergence in insulin/IGF1 and GPCR-mediated pancreatic cancer cell proliferation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the signaling mechanisms that mediate the biological responses eliciting by the insulin/IGFs and GPCRs in pancreatic cancer cells are complex and involve multiple signaling systems.

the mTOR pathway represents a critical node in the insulin/IGFs-GPCR signaling network and that the mTOR inhibitor rapamycin and its derivatives represent a promising class of agents to target PDAC cells.
targeting mTOR may be an effective strategy to prevent PDAC and that metformin, an inexpensive, well tolerated and readily available drug, may be a promising chemopreventive agent for PDAC.
